leftEvidence.title: Noah receives warning and ship instructions

points.label: Noah-relative action
points.left: God tells Noah that violence has brought an end to all flesh, then specifies the ship, its rooms, dimensions, covering, occupants, animals, and food.
points.right: The writer compares a mother enduring her children’s torment to Noah’s ship bearing up in the world-filling flood.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Noah does everything God commands after receiving a covenant announcement about entering with his household.
points.right: Flood, waves, storms, and preservation become poetic language for disciplined endurance.

payload.posture: Genesis describes Noah building a ship for preservation; 4 Maccabees turns that ship into an analogy for a mother enduring overwhelming grief.

rightEvidence.title: Noah’s ship becomes an image of endurance

payload.tension: The analogy depends on the ship’s flood setting without making the two human stories identical.
payload.title: The commanded ship and a later endurance image
